exercise.name: Old School Reverse Extensions
aliases: Reverse hyperextension (on a table or box)
Prone straight-leg raise off a box

reference.title: Old School Reverse Extensions
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be read at authoring time, so the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice)

equipment: Plyo box or sturdy high table
exercise.mechanics: Isolation (hip extension with straight legs, prone on a raised surface)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the legs rise, in as they lower.

prescription.tempo: About 1 s up, short squeeze, 1.5 s down
prescription.progression: Longer squeeze at the top, then ankle weights, then a reverse hyper machine

cues.text: Lie face down on a high box with the hips at the edge and the legs hanging, toes near the floor; hold the sides of the box.
Squeeze the glutes and lift both straight legs until they are level with the body.
Short squeeze; do not arch past level.
Lower the legs slowly back down.
Toes near the floor, then the next rep.

mistakes.fix: Lift with the glutes, pause, and lower slowly.
Stop with the legs in line with the body.
Keep the legs long (or slightly soft).

mistakes.mistake: Hips on top of the box
mistakes.fix: Hips at the edge so they can move freely.

kinematics.norm: From about 50-70 degrees (legs hanging) to about 0 degrees, legs level (clinical opinion)
About level at the top (clinical opinion)
Chest and belly stay on the box; prone hip extension recruits the glutes and lumbar extensors (Kim 2014; Macadam and Feser 2019)
About 1 s up and 1.5 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual 11401, Old School Reverse Extensions, video (movement reference)
Kim et al. 2014, selective activation of lumbar paraspinal muscles during exercises in the prone position (J Phys Ther Sci 26(8):1223-1224)
Macadam and Feser 2019, gluteus maximus EMG excitation during dynamic body-weight hip extension: a systematic review (Int J Sports Phys Ther 14(1):14-31; PMC6350668)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Use a box or table that is stable and will not slide; pad the edge under the hips.
Low-back pain: keep the top short of level and avoid arching.
modify: Smaller range (legs to just below level).
regressions: Prone straight-leg hip extension on the floor.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Gluteus maximus extends the hip and lifts the straight leg; prone hip extension recruits it well (Macadam and Feser 2019).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Gluteus maximus extends the hip and lifts the straight leg (Macadam and Feser 2019).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Help extend the hip and keep the knee long.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Help extend the hip and keep the knee long.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Lumbar extensors fix the pelvis at the top; prone leg lifts activate them (Kim 2014).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Lumbar extensors fix the pelvis at the top (Kim 2014).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Pull the body onto the box.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Pull the body onto the box.
muscleNotes.core: Holds the trunk still on the box.
